reasoning: An old Turkish-route loan, said darzan with two short a vowels. Normal in Ramallah markets for a dozen.
ق is a glottal stop even in this school-register word. Taa marbuta after ر is a.
ح is 7 and the taa marbuta after م is e. One bird of the collective 7amaam, covering both pigeon and dove.
د is a sun letter, so the article assimilates to id-. doktoor is the everyday word for a physician in Ramallah, ahead of Tabiib.
ما negates the possessive il-, as the dialect rules require. Literally there is no call for it, used for unnecessary or pointless.
ظ is the emphatic TH. The verb reading is THahar, appeared; the same letters as a noun would be Duhur, noon.
ط is emphatic T and the medial hamza is a glottal stop. The English abbreviation is vague: a Taa'ife is a sect or confessional community, not a branch in any general sense.
ث becomes t in urban Palestinian, exactly as ثالث becomes تالت, so ثامن is respelled تامن.
The adjective reading is 3afin, mouldy or gone off; the doubled verb 3affan would be to go mouldy. Of food, msawwis or kharbaan is also heard.
khalliina plus the bare imperfect is the Palestinian let us construction. Both verbs are form II, so the shadda doubles ل and ل respectively.
The hamza is no longer word-initial once the article is attached, so it is written: il-'arjantiina. Many speakers say il-'arjantiin without the final a.
ج assimilates the article in Levantine, giving ij-jum3a. Taa marbuta after ع is a.
Country name borrowed with long uu and ii and a glide before the final a. Vowel length here varies by speaker.
Word-initial hamza on a vowel seat is not written, just the long ii. ط is emphatic T, and the ending is a glide plus a, not -iya.
ع is a moon letter so the article stays il- after bi-. In Levantine this really does mean barely or with great effort, distinct from the good-health wish 3aafye.
Word-initial hamza on an alif seat is written as the bare vowel. ض is emphatic D. Covers the floor indoors and the ground or land outside.
Long oo in the first syllable, not uu. The ordinary Ramallah adjective for hungry.
ط is emphatic T and ق glottalises even here, as in mish manTi'i. Used in everyday argument, not only in writing.
The cluster is broken by a second u, shughul, rather than MSA shughl.
mish is the right negator before an adjective. ط is emphatic T and ع is 3. Often used admiringly, meaning unbelievable.
Taa marbuta after ل is e. The everyday word in Ramallah; hazze arDiyye is the news register.
7akeet with the long ee plus the indirect object -lu. ع reduces to 3a and the article assimilates to the sun letter ت.
In the construct the first taa marbuta is pronounced t, so it is respelled ت. salle has shadda on ل and a final e.
Taa marbuta after س is e. A daily conversation word in Ramallah, so Palestinian despite its MSA shape.
French ascenseur, with the long ee written as kasra on the ي. The word-initial hamza seat is just the vowel. maS3ad is the formal alternative nobody uses in speech.
